analysis.title: GUT CHECK
key_insights: Last week neither NVDA's strong earnings and guidance nor the $93.5B IPO, the largest in market history, acted as a clearing event. Price action was deflating.
Futures bounced Monday AM after supportive comments from the Trump administration on NVDA over the weekend.
Asia announced market support: China lowered margin requirements, Korea eased buyback restrictions, Taiwan tightened short selling rules.
Rene Haas, a lead contender for NVDA's next CEO, reaffirmed his commitment to Arm with a new employment agreement through 2033 and will become vice chairman of Softbank.
Global Fundamental L/S managers lost 1.2% (-1.8 SD) on Friday 11/20, down 2.1% MTD and up 7% YTD. US-focused funds lost 1.6% (-2.6 SD), down 2.9% MTD and up 3.6% YTD.
Systematic L/S managers were flat Friday with 60% finishing lower, up 1.5% MTD and 17.7% YTD.
After 5 weeks of de-grossing, HFs re-grossed by the largest amount in 4+ years. The book was net sold as short selling outpaced long buying, with aggressive macro product hedging.

PB long/short ratio fell to the lowest on GS records. All regions were net sold, EM for 10 straight weeks, and 10 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Financials. Energy was the only net bought sector.
Buyback desk volumes were 2.2x the 2025 YTD ADTV and 2.4x the 2024 YTD ADTV, skewed to Industrials, Financials and Consumer Discretionary. Corporates are the most consistent US equity buyer in 2026.
S&P 500 is down 12% from its Oct 6 record high (-8.61% last week). After 22 prior 10% corrections since 1980, the index averaged +4% over the next 3 months and rose in 17 (73%).
S&P 500 forward P/E is down 25% YTD to 16x, near the historical average. Trend-earnings valuations remain elevated, with the CAPE on trend earnings at the 83rd percentile since 1990.

AI boom lifted S&P 500 earnings about 25% above the 30-year trend, creating downside risk as capex tailwinds fade. Investors focus on medium-term earnings uncertainty despite Q3 EPS growth above 30% y/y.
HFs and MFs share overweights in HC, Industrials and Financials and mechanical TMT underweights. They disagree on Consumer Discretionary (HFs overweight) and Consumer Staples (HFs underweight).

market_movers.rationale: Strong earnings and guidance did not stabilize the market, but supportive Trump administration comments lifted futures Monday.
